Category. minor (sometimes called the half-diminished mode)

Differentiating scale degree: b5th

For chord types: diminished; m7>5

Locrian outlines the basic structure of a minor seventh flat five chord (root. 3rd, b5th, b7th) and these extensions: 9th, 11th, and © 13th.

Pattems for Locrian

(Roots are circled; notes in parentheses are the b5th degrees.)

Fig. 21

Locrian is the seventh mode of the major scale. It corresponds to the vii chord in major keys, but it is most often relegated to the ii7'5 chords in minor key progressions. When played out of context, it's a very strange sounding scale indeed. But when mated with a minor seven flat five chord, it nails all of the chord tones and provides some choice alterations (>9th and 513th). Fig. 22
